headline: SpaceX, which includes Elon Musk's xAI, has agreed to send a representative to the New York City Council on Friday to answer questions on AI safety, after being served with a subpoena.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a city council forced a major AI company to agree to appear, per the Council Speaker and several outlets, but it is a hearing, not a law.
importance_line: New Yorkers, whose Council is holding hearings on AI safety, and AI companies face a test of whether a city can make a firm appear and answer, but SpaceX has only agreed to send someone and it is unclear who will speak or what they will say.
summary: The New York Post reports, citing Council Speaker Julie Menin, that SpaceX, which includes Elon Musk's xAI artificial intelligence unit, agreed on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 to send a representative to the New York City Council on Friday to answer questions on AI safety risks, after ignoring a subpoena issued on 28 Sep 2026 and skipping the Council's 5 Oct hearing, where Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta took part. Menin said "self-regulation is not enough", the Post says it is unclear who will speak for SpaceX, and our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the Associated Press report on the 5 Oct hearing.
notes: CNBC page (pool source) gave an access error (HTTP 403); story read at the New York Post (https://nypost.com/2026/10/13/business/elon-musks-spacex-set-to-testify-at-nyc-council-hearing-on-ai-safety-after-getting-subpoena/) and checked against International Business Times UK (https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/elon-musks-spacex-finally-agrees-testify-after-nyc-council-brands-their-absence-unacceptable-1825337), which gives Friday 16 Oct, 10am Eastern. Follow-up of the 5 Oct hearing (our 6 Oct 2026 edition); the agreement itself is new, so NEW.
